subject: maths
title: Telling the Time to 5 Minutes
seo_title: Year 2 Telling the Time Worksheets: O’clock, Quarter Past and 5 Minutes (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Compare and sequence intervals of time; tell and write the time to five minutes, including quarter past/to the hour and draw the hands on a clock face to show these times; know the number of minutes in an hour and the number of hours in a day.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on telling the time: o’clock, half past, quarter past and quarter to, then 5-minute times past and to the hour, minutes in an hour, hours in a day, and comparing and ordering times. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Short hand: the hour. Long hand: count in 5s for the minutes.
key_sub: Long hand on the right-hand side: minutes past. On the left-hand side: minutes to the next hour, so 25 to 9 is 8:35.
body_html:
The two hands

A clock has two hands. The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes. Each number is 5 minutes for the long hand, so count in 5s.

O’clock, half past, quarter past and quarter to

Long hand onWe sayDigital
127 o’clock7:00
3quarter past 77:15
6half past 77:30
9quarter to 87:45

Past and to

Long hand on the right-hand side: say minutes past the hour. Long hand on the left-hand side: say minutes to the next hour. Count in 5s back to the 12.

Read the clock

The long hand points to the 10. The short hand is between 4 and 5.

The 10 is on the left-hand side, so say “to”. Count back to the 12: 5, 10. The next hour is 5.

Answer: 10 to 5

Draw the hands

Show 25 past 6 on a clock.

Long hand: count in 5s to 25. That is the 5. Short hand: just under half way from the 6 to the 7.

Answer: Long hand on the 5, short hand between 6 and 7

Time facts

TimeEquals
1 hour60 minutes
half an hour30 minutes
a quarter of an hour15 minutes
1 day24 hours

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
“25 to 9” read as 9:3525 to 9 is before 9 o’clock. The short hand has not reached 9, so it is 8:35.
Long hand on the 4 read as 4 minutesEach number is 5 minutes: 5, 10, 15, 20. It is 20 past.
Past and to mixed upRight-hand side: past. Left-hand side: to.
Quarter to 6 written as 6:45Quarter to 6 is 15 minutes before 6 o’clock: 5:45.

faq.q: What time should a Year 2 child be able to tell?
faq.a: By the end of Year 2, children should tell and write the time to 5 minutes, including quarter past and quarter to, and draw the hands on a clock to show these times.

faq.q: How many minutes are in an hour and hours in a day?
faq.a: There are 60 minutes in 1 hour and 24 hours in 1 day. Year 2 children are expected to know both facts.

faq.q: Why do children say “25 to 9” for 8:35?
faq.a: When the long hand is on the left-hand side of the clock, we count the minutes back to the next hour. 8:35 is 25 minutes before 9 o’clock, so it is 25 to 9.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn to tell the time?
faq.a: Use an analogue clock at home and ask the time at everyday moments, such as breakfast or bedtime. Practise counting in 5s round the clock, then move from o’clock and half past to quarter past, quarter to and 5-minute times.

sets.title: O’clock, half past, quarter past and quarter to

items.e: The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 3. So it is 3 o’clock. (The long hand on the 12 does not mean 12 o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 9. So it is 9 o’clock. (The long hand on the 12 does not mean 12 o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 8. So it is 8 o’clock. (The long hand on the 12 does not mean 12 o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 6: half way round, so it is half past. The short hand is between 9 and 10. The short hand has not reached the 10 yet, so the hour is still 9. It is half past 9.
The long hand points to the 6: half way round, so it is half past. The short hand is between 1 and 2. The short hand has not reached the 2 yet, so the hour is still 1. It is half past 1.
The long hand points to the 6: half way round, so it is half past. The short hand is between 7 and 8. The short hand has not reached the 8 yet, so the hour is still 7. It is half past 7.
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round, so it is quarter past. The short hand is between 1 and 2. The short hand has just passed the 1. It is quarter past 1.
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round, so it is quarter past. The short hand is between 8 and 9. The short hand has just passed the 8. It is quarter past 8.
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round, so it is quarter past. The short hand is between 11 and 12. The short hand has just passed the 11. It is quarter past 11.

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12, so it is quarter to. The short hand is between 10 and 11. The short hand is nearly at the 11, but not there yet. In 15 more minutes it will be 11 o’clock. So it is quarter to 11.

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12, so it is quarter to. The short hand is between 3 and 4. The short hand is nearly at the 4, but not there yet. In 15 more minutes it will be 4 o’clock. So it is quarter to 4.

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12, so it is quarter to. The short hand is between 6 and 7. The short hand is nearly at the 7, but not there yet. In 15 more minutes it will be 7 o’clock. So it is quarter to 7.

items.q: At half past, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Half past means the long hand has gone half way round the clock, from the 12 to the 6.

items.q: At quarter past, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Quarter past means the long hand has gone a quarter of the way round, from the 12 to the 3. (The 9 is for quarter to.)

items.q: At quarter to, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Quarter to means a quarter of an hour before the 12. The long hand points to the 9. (The 3 is for quarter past.)

items.q: At half past 2, where is the short hand?
items.e: In half an hour the short hand moves half way to the next number. At half past 2 it is between 2 and 3.

items.q: Quarter past 6 is how many minutes after 6 o’clock?
items.e: A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 3: 5, 10, 15. (3 is the number, not the minutes.)

items.q: Quarter to 6 is how many minutes before 6 o’clock?
items.e: Quarter to 6 is a quarter of an hour before 6 o’clock. That is 15 minutes. Count in 5s back from the 12 to the 9: 5, 10, 15.

items.q: Which digital time is the same as half past 3?
items.e: Half past 3 is 30 minutes after 3 o’clock. On a digital clock it is 3:30. (Not 4:30: the hour is still 3.)

items.q: Which digital time is the same as quarter to 6?
items.e: Quarter to 6 is 15 minutes before 6 o’clock, so it is still in the 5 o’clock hour: 45 minutes past 5. That is 5:45. (6:45 is quarter to 7.)

sets.title: Times to 5 minutes: past the hour

items.q: The long hand points to the 2. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 2: 5, 10. It is 10 minutes past. (Not 2 minutes: the number is not the minutes.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 4. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 4: 5, 10, 15, 20. It is 20 minutes past. (Not 4 minutes: the number is not the minutes.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 1. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 1: 5. It is 5 minutes past. (Not 1 minute: the number is not the minutes.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 5. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. It is 25 minutes past. (Not 5 minutes: the number is not the minutes.)

The long hand points to the 2. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes past. The short hand is between 11 and 12. So it is 10 past 11. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.
The long hand points to the 1. Count in 5s from the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes past. The short hand is between 4 and 5. So it is 5 past 4. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

The long hand points to the 4. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes past. The short hand is between 1 and 2. So it is 20 past 1. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

The long hand points to the 5. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes past. The short hand is between 1 and 2. So it is 25 past 1. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

The long hand points to the 4. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes past. The short hand is between 7 and 8. So it is 20 past 7. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.
The long hand points to the 2. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes past. The short hand is between 8 and 9. So it is 10 past 8. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

The long hand points to the 5. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes past. The short hand is between 3 and 4. So it is 25 past 3. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.
The long hand points to the 1. Count in 5s from the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes past. The short hand is between 2 and 3. So it is 5 past 2. The long hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past.

items.q: At 25 past 3, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count in 5s from the 12 until you say 25: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 5 numbers, so the long hand points to the 5. (The 7 on the other side is for 25 to.)

items.q: At 10 past 7, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count in 5s from the 12 until you say 10: 5, 10. That is 2 numbers, so the long hand points to the 2. (The 10 on the other side is for 10 to.)

items.q: At 20 past 11, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count in 5s from the 12 until you say 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 numbers, so the long hand points to the 4. (The 8 on the other side is for 20 to.)

items.q: At 5 past 4, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count in 5s from the 12 until you say 5: 5. That is 1 number, so the long hand points to the 1. (The 11 on the other side is for 5 to.)

sets.title: Times to 5 minutes: to the hour

items.q: The long hand points to the 11. How many minutes is it to the next hour?
items.e: Count in 5s back from the 11 to the 12: 5. It is 5 minutes to the hour. (55 minutes is how many minutes past.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 8. How many minutes is it to the next hour?
items.e: Count in 5s back from the 8 to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. It is 20 minutes to the hour. (40 minutes is how many minutes past.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 10. How many minutes is it to the next hour?
items.e: Count in 5s back from the 10 to the 12: 5, 10. It is 10 minutes to the hour. (50 minutes is how many minutes past.)

items.q: The long hand points to the 7. How many minutes is it to the next hour?
items.e: Count in 5s back from the 7 to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. It is 25 minutes to the hour. (35 minutes is how many minutes past.)

The long hand points to the 10. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes to. The short hand is between 1 and 2, nearly at the 2. So it is 10 to 2. (It is not 10 to 1: the next hour is 2.)

The long hand points to the 8. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes to. The short hand is between 2 and 3, nearly at the 3. So it is 20 to 3. (It is not 20 to 2: the next hour is 3.)
The long hand points to the 11. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes to. The short hand is between 6 and 7, nearly at the 7. So it is 5 to 7. (It is not 5 to 6: the next hour is 7.)

The long hand points to the 7. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes to. The short hand is between 12 and 1, nearly at the 1. So it is 25 to 1. (It is not 25 to 12: the next hour is 1.)

The long hand points to the 10. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes to. The short hand is between 11 and 12, nearly at the 12. So it is 10 to 12. (It is not 10 to 11: the next hour is 12.)

The long hand points to the 8. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes to. The short hand is between 3 and 4, nearly at the 4. So it is 20 to 4. (It is not 20 to 3: the next hour is 4.)
The long hand points to the 11. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes to. The short hand is between 8 and 9, nearly at the 9. So it is 5 to 9. (It is not 5 to 8: the next hour is 9.)

The long hand points to the 7. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes to. The short hand is between 1 and 2, nearly at the 2. So it is 25 to 2. (It is not 25 to 1: the next hour is 2.)

The long hand points to the 8. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes to. The short hand is between 12 and 1, nearly at the 1. So it is 20 to 1. (It is not 20 to 12: the next hour is 1.)

The long hand points to the 7. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes to. The short hand is between 5 and 6, nearly at the 6. So it is 25 to 6. (It is not 25 to 5: the next hour is 6.)

The long hand points to the 10. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes to. The short hand is between 2 and 3, nearly at the 3. So it is 10 to 3. (It is not 10 to 2: the next hour is 3.)
The long hand points to the 11. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes to. The short hand is between 1 and 2, nearly at the 2. So it is 5 to 2. (It is not 5 to 1: the next hour is 2.)

items.q: Which digital time is the same as 25 to 9?
items.e: 25 to 9 is 25 minutes before 9 o’clock, so it is still in the 8 o’clock hour. 60 − 25 = 35 minutes past 8: 8:35. (9:35 is 35 minutes after 9 o’clock.)

items.q: Which digital time is the same as 10 to 3?
items.e: 10 to 3 is 10 minutes before 3 o’clock, so it is still in the 2 o’clock hour. 60 − 10 = 50 minutes past 2: 2:50. (3:50 is 50 minutes after 3 o’clock.)

items.q: At 10 to 4, where does the long hand point?
items.e: 10 to means 10 minutes before the 12. Count back in 5s from the 12: 5, 10. The long hand points to the 10. (The 2 is for 10 past.)

items.q: At 20 to 7, where does the long hand point?
items.e: 20 to means 20 minutes before the 12. Count back in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. The long hand points to the 8. (The 4 is for 20 past.)

sets.title: Which clock? Minutes, hours and days

items.e: The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round, so it is quarter past. The short hand is between 1 and 2. Clock A shows quarter past 1.
There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. The long hand goes all the way round: 12 numbers × 5 = 60. (Not 100.)
The long hand points to the 4. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes past. The short hand is between 10 and 11. Clock B shows 20 past 10.
There are 24 hours in 1 day. The short hand goes round the clock twice: 12 + 12 = 24.

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12, so it is quarter to. The short hand is between 6 and 7. Clock C shows quarter to 7. (Clock A shows quarter to 8, not quarter to 7: its short hand is past the 7.)

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30. (Not 50: an hour is not 100 minutes.)

The long hand points to the 7. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes to. The short hand is between 8 and 9. Clock D shows 25 to 9. (Clock B shows 25 to 10, not 25 to 9: its short hand is past the 9.)

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. A quarter of 60 is 15. The long hand goes from the 12 to the 3: 5, 10, 15.

The long hand points to the 10. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10. That is 10 minutes to. The short hand is between 2 and 3. Clock B shows 10 to 3. (Clock D shows 10 to 4, not 10 to 3: its short hand is past the 3.)

items.q: The long hand goes all the way round once. How long is that?
items.e: Each number is 5 minutes, and there are 12 numbers: 60 minutes. 60 minutes is 1 hour.
The long hand points to the 1. Count in 5s from the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes past. The short hand is between 5 and 6. Clock C shows 5 past 5.

items.q: Which is the same as 1 day?
items.e: 1 day is 24 hours. (12 hours is only half a day.)
The long hand points to the 6: half way round, so it is half past. The short hand is between 11 and 12. Clock D shows half past 11.

items.q: The long hand moves from the 12 to the 6. How many minutes go by?
items.e: Count in 5s for each number: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. 30 minutes go by. That is half an hour.

The long hand points to the 8. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 minutes to. The short hand is between 12 and 1. Clock A shows 20 to 1. (Clock C shows 20 to 2, not 20 to 1: its short hand is past the 1.)

items.q: The long hand moves from the 3 to the 6. How many minutes go by?
items.e: From the 3 to the 6 is 3 numbers. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. 15 minutes go by.
The long hand points to the 5. Count in 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25 minutes past. The short hand is between 9 and 10. Clock C shows 25 past 9.

items.q: How many hours are in half a day?
items.e: 1 day is 24 hours. Half of 24 is 12 hours. (30 is half an hour in minutes.)

The long hand points to the 11. Count in 5s back to the 12: 5. That is 5 minutes to. The short hand is between 7 and 8. Clock B shows 5 to 8. (Clock A shows 5 to 9, not 5 to 8: its short hand is past the 8.)
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday: 7 days. (5 is just the school days.)
Brushing teeth, eating an apple and putting on shoes take a few minutes. A night’s sleep takes many hours. So a night’s sleep takes the longest.

items.q: About how long does a film at the cinema last?
items.e: 2 minutes is far too short, and 2 days or 20 hours is far too long. A film lasts about 2 hours.
1 hour is 60 minutes. 60 is more than 45. So 1 hour is longer.
Quarter of an hour = 15 minutes. Half an hour = 30 minutes. 1 hour = 60 minutes. 15 is the smallest, so quarter of an hour is the shortest.
Quarter to 8 is 15 minutes before 8 o’clock. The others are 8 o’clock or later. So quarter to 8 is the earliest.
25 to 5 is 4:35. 20 past 4 is 4:20 and quarter past 4 is 4:15. 4:35 is the latest, so the answer is 25 to 5.

items.q: What comes next? 3 o’clock, quarter past 3, half past 3, …
items.e: Each time is 15 minutes later. 15 minutes after half past 3 is quarter to 4.

items.q: What comes next? 5 past 2, 10 past 2, quarter past 2, …
items.e: Each time is 5 minutes later. 5 minutes after quarter past 2 (15 past) is 20 past 2.

items.q: It is 4 o’clock. What time will it be 1 hour later?
items.e: 1 hour later, the short hand moves on one number, from 4 to 5. It will be 5 o’clock.

items.q: It is half past 6. What time will it be 1 hour later?
items.e: 1 hour later, the hour goes up by 1 and the minutes stay the same. Half past 6 → half past 7.

items.q: Oliver has tea at 5 o’clock. It is 4 o’clock now. How long until tea?
items.e: From 4 o’clock to 5 o’clock the short hand moves on one number. That is 1 hour.

items.q: Lunchtime starts at 12 o’clock and ends at half past 12. How long is lunchtime?
items.e: The long hand moves from the 12 to the 6. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Lunchtime is 30 minutes.

items.q: A TV programme starts at 4 o’clock and ends at quarter past 4. How long is it?
items.e: The long hand moves from the 12 to the 3. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. It is 15 minutes long. (3 is the number, not the minutes.)

items.q: A film starts at 5 o’clock. It lasts 2 hours. When does it end?
items.e: Count on 2 hours: 5 o’clock → 6 o’clock → 7 o’clock. (3 o’clock is 2 hours before.)

items.q: Jack’s swimming lesson starts at quarter past 4. It lasts half an hour. When does it end?
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. Quarter past 4 is 4:15. 4:15 + 30 minutes = 4:45. That is quarter to 5. (Quarter to 4 is before the lesson starts.)

items.q: George puts a cake in the oven at 2 o’clock. It is ready 20 minutes later. When is it ready?
items.e: Count on 20 minutes from 2 o’clock: the long hand moves from the 12 to the 4 (5, 10, 15, 20). It is ready at 20 past 2. (20 to 2 is before 2 o’clock.)

items.q: Alfie gets to the bus stop at 20 to 9. The bus comes at 10 to 9. How long does he wait?
items.e: 20 to 9 is 8:40. 10 to 9 is 8:50. From 8:40 to 8:50 is 10 minutes. (Do not add 20 and 10.)

items.q: Charlie reads for 20 minutes. Grace reads for half an hour. Who reads for longer, and by how much?
c: They read for the same time
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. 30 is more than 20, and 30 − 20 = 10. So Grace reads for longer, by 10 minutes.

items.q: Put these times in order, earliest first.
c: half past 3, quarter past 3, quarter to 4
quarter past 3, quarter to 4, half past 3
quarter past 3, half past 3, quarter to 4
quarter to 4, quarter past 3, half past 3
items.e: Quarter past 3 is 3:15. Half past 3 is 3:30. Quarter to 4 is 3:45. So the order is quarter past 3, half past 3, quarter to 4. (Quarter to 4 comes last: it is nearly 4 o’clock.)
The clock shows 10 past 4. Count on 20 minutes: 10 past, 15 past, 20 past, 25 past, half past. She finishes at half past 4.
